idiom_name: interface delegation (by) with a per-gate check; function-type handlers or Ktor plugins for pipelines
implementation_notes: Kotlin generates the forwarding a proxy class would hand-write: class Gate(private val next: Service) : Service by next delegates every member to the inner service, and the gate overrides only the member it must guard, checking and then calling the delegate - the same shape works for suspend service interfaces. What replaces the classic structure: the by-clause (plus function types and Ktor's plugin pipeline for HTTP) replaces the proxy class and the hand-built chain, so the boilerplate disappears but the check itself and its evidence remain yours; keep the verified identity in the call attributes or the coroutine context and re-verify it at each gate, because delegation changes who forwards, not who trusts. The hand-written form is still justified when the guarded interface is generic or a platform type whose members must be guarded individually.
pitfalls: Because by forwards everything, a member the gate forgets to override is passed through unchecked; review the gate whenever the interface grows.
Members overridden in the delegating class are not called from the delegate's own code (the delegate only sees itself), so checks must not rely on the inner service calling back.
A coroutine-context element carrying the verified identity is inherited by child coroutines; launching work outside the gate's scope either drops the identity or leaks it into unrelated work.
